fields.quote: "i don't think we can reliably safeguard against users shooting themselves in the foot. best we can do is warn people." (owner, 2026-11-07); "a schedule can run anything. who cares?" (owner, 2026-11-07). The agent's proposed defaults (warnings never block; schedules per repo in rhiza.toml, run once after downtime, skip a slot while the previous run is going) were accepted by the owner ("go ahead").
fields.statement: Rhiza does not try to safeguard owners against risky setups (such as an autonomous workflow with bypassPermissions fed by outside input); it warns plainly, in rhiza health, workflow check and the guides, and leaves the choice to the owner. A schedule can run anything: a workflow or a plain command.
